title: Moules Marinières
subtitle: Mussels steamed in white wine with shallots and parsley
excerpt: Live mussels steamed open in a wine-and-shallot broth with butter and parsley. The broth is as important as the mussels: the wine and mussel liquor combine into something you'll want to soak up with crusty bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moules marinières (sailor-style mussels) is the classic French-Belgian preparation of mussels and is most associated with Normandy and the coastal regions of Belgium, where mussels have been farmed since at least the 13th century. The dish is simple: mussels steamed in white wine with shallots, butter, and parsley. Belgium serves them with frites; France often serves them alone with bread. Mussels are at their best from September to April, when they are cold-water plump and briny.

recipeTools.notes: Must have a tight-fitting lid. The pan needs to be large enough to hold all the mussels with room to steam.

content.text: Discard any mussels that are open before cooking and do not close when you tap them firmly: these are dead and should not be eaten. Pull off the beards (the straggly dark fibres at the join of the shell) with a sharp tug. Scrub the shells if they are sandy. The cooking takes under 5 minutes from the moment the lid goes on: mussels are done as soon as their shells open. Overcooking makes them tough and rubbery.

items.preparation: scrubbed, beards removed, open ones discarded

content.text: Melt the butter in a large pan with a lid over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 4 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Pour in the wine and bring to a boil. Add the mussels, put the lid on, and cook over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until all the shells are open. Discard any that remain closed.

Lift the mussels out with a slotted spoon into warm bowls. If using cream, stir it through the broth and heat for 30 seconds. Add the parsley and pepper to the broth. Pour the broth over the mussels. Serve with crusty bread.
